title: Routh–Hurwitz stability
equipment: Rigid rotary shaft with viscous friction
physicalPurpose: Use the continuous-time stability prediction to choose a bounded proportional shaft trial.
objective: Interpret the Routh table for s²+s+Kp, then compare stable, boundary and unstable shaft responses.

simplifications: The angle and velocity thresholds command zero torque and Manual mode; they are not mechanical travel hard-stops
Continuous model predicts poles while ST updates every 20 ms

baseline.limitation: A finite command error with Kp=0 does not establish asymptotic stability.

change.decision: Apply Kp=1 after the Routh first column predicts Kp>0.

acceptance.window: 10 s after 0→0.01 rad step at Kp=1
after angle or velocity safety limit at Kp=-1

abortPredicates: Angle reaches ±0.2 rad or velocity reaches ±2 rad/s; the controller commands zero torque and Manual mode
Required signal is nonfinite or invalid
safety.restorationMode: Disable the experiment, confirm zero torque and Manual mode, then restart the simulator to reset angle and velocity. The thresholds do not model mechanical travel hard-stops.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised motion-controls engineer and responsible machine operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: This lesson cannot authorise physical servo gain application

video.viewerOutcome: Read the Routh first column, select Kp and compare the bounded shaft responses.

learning.context: A simulated J=B=1 shaft is controlled by u=Kp(r-theta).
learning.reason: The root locus supplies selected gains but does not state the complete stability interval.
theory: For the declared plant 1/[s(s+1)] and proportional controller Kp, the characteristic polynomial is s²+s+Kp.
The Routh first column is 1, 1, Kp, so asymptotic stability requires Kp>0.
Kp=0 has an origin pole and Kp=-1 has one right-half-plane pole.
learning.workedPrediction: Predict decay at Kp=1, finite command error at Kp=0, and growth toward the stop threshold at Kp=-1.
practicalPreparation: Confirm zero angle and velocity, 20 ms task period and ±20 N·m actuator bound.
Use the 0.01 rad step and record angle, velocity and torque for 10 s.
learning.baseline: At Kp=0 the shaft remains at zero while the 0.01 rad command error remains finite.
learning.change: Apply Kp=1 from the Routh interval.
learning.comparison: Change only Kp between -1, 0 and 1 while keeping the plant, reset and step fixed.
learning.validation: Kp=1 decays, Kp=0 remains unmoved, and Kp=-1 grows before zero-torque Manual restoration.
learning.explanation: The continuous Routh prediction does not remove sampled execution, saturation or stop-threshold assumptions.
learning.transfer: Periodic excitation next measures response to continuing inputs at selected rates.
